hook.text: Five thousand years ago, Egyptians strapped a cloth to a pole on a reed boat. Global trade began.

buildup.text: Sails turned wind into forward motion. No rowing crew needed. Ships could finally cross open water.

discovery.text: Phoenicians refined sail design and navigated the entire Mediterranean using stars and coastal landmarks.

twist.text: Wind is free but unpredictable. Voyages could take weeks longer than planned—or never finish.

climax.text: For 4,500 years, wind was the only power available at sea. Steam didn't arrive until the 1800s.

punchline.text: A piece of cloth powered global trade for millennia.

quiz.question: Who were among the first to navigate the open Mediterranean by sail?
